title: Probing La-based nickelates with Ni 1$s$ core-level photoelectron spectroscopy
authors: Daisuke Takegami, Naoki Ito, Koto Fujinuma, Masato Yoshimura, Grace A. Pan, Dan Ferenc Segedin, Qi Song, Hanjong Paik, Charles M. Brooks, Hanjie Guo, Alexander C. Komarek, Takanori Taniguchi, Masaki Fujita, Julia A. Mundy, Takashi Mizokawa, Liu Hao Tjeng, Berit H. Goodge, Atsushi Hariki
abstract: We present a comparative Ni core level photoemission study of La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$, Nd$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$, and LaNiO$_3$ using both the Ni $2p$ and the Ni $1s$. We address the challenges in analyzing the widely investigated Ni $2p$ spectra arising from the substantial overlap in energy of the Ni $2p$ with the La $3d$. We show that on the other hand the deep Ni $1s$ core level does provide a clean view on the intrinsic electronic excitations and we highlight its potential to resolve detailed differences in the electronic structure within the strongly correlated Ruddlesden-Popper series La$_{n+1}$Ni$_n$O$_{3n+1}$.
summary: This work compares Ni 1s and Ni 2p photoelectron spectra across various La-based nickelates to probe their electronic structure. The authors argue that the deeper Ni 1s core level offers a clearer view of intrinsic correlations by avoiding spectral overlaps present in the more commonly used Ni 2p measurement. By combining experiment with DFT+DMFT calculations, they successfully map material differences onto changes in fundamental electronic parameters.
main_problem: The study addresses the challenge of accurately determining the electronic structure of La-based nickelates by comparing core-level photoemission spectra from different Ni core levels.
main_result: The deep Ni 1s core level provides a cleaner view of intrinsic electronic excitations compared to the Ni 2p level, which suffers from spectral overlap with the La 3d states. This allows for distinguishing material variations within the Ruddlesden-Popper series.
method: The research combines experimental Hard X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (HAXPES) measurements with theoretical calculations using Density Functional Theory combined with Dynamical Mean-Field Theory (DFT+DMFT).
model_or_system: The physical system is the Ruddlesden-Popper series of nickelates, including La3Ni2O7, Nd3Ni2O7, and LaNiO3. The analysis focuses on the electronic correlation effects within these layered perovskite structures.
key_observables: Core-level binding energies (Ni 1s vs Ni 2p), spectral line shapes, satellite features, and intensity ratios.
important_parameters: Charge transfer energy ($\Delta_{dp}$), hybridization strength ($V(\epsilon)$), and the specific stoichiometry of the nickelate layers.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the Ni 1s spectrum is less contaminated by neighboring orbitals compared to the Ni 2p spectrum, allowing it to probe intrinsic electronic correlations.
figures_summary: Figures compare Ni 1s and Ni 2p spectra across different nickelates (e.g., Nd3Ni2O7 vs La3Ni2O7), demonstrating spectral overlaps in Ni 2p and showing material-dependent variations in the cleaner Ni 1s spectrum.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first identifying the spectroscopic limitations of the Ni 2p level due to overlap, then presenting evidence from Ni 1s measurements that it is a viable alternative. Finally, theoretical calculations are used to model how changes in electronic parameters ($\Delta_{dp}$, hybridization) account for observed spectral differences between related compounds.
why_interesting: The detailed spectroscopic analysis of strongly correlated nickelates using core-level photoemission spectroscopy provides direct experimental constraints on the effective Hamiltonians and correlation strengths used in theoretical models like DMFT, which is highly relevant to understanding high-Tc superconductivity mechanisms.
